thread:
Marta: Heads-up — saw repeated warm-pool failures in us-west2 when dedicated capacity hit the soft quota. Lots of fallbacks to shared causing latency and cost spikes.
Josh: When did this start? any reproducible jobs?
Marta: Started ~09:12 PT. warm-pool hit and warm latency p95 jumped from ~40ms -> ~280ms, error 429s creeping up.
Carlos: That's the region where we disabled prefill to save on committed spend, so dedicated slices are tighter.
Priya: Are we spilling cross-region or within-region? Router policy matters.
Marta: Current router allows regional shared fallback, but shared nodes in us-west2 are already saturated, so router is spilling to eu-west1 and routing back — causing egress and double token charges.
Josh: Ugh — cross-region fallback is the hidden cost. Latency + egress cost adds up quickly. We should prefer local degraded variants before crossing regions.
Priya: Agreed. Proposal: change routing priority to prefer local quantized/degraded model variants first, then local shared, then cross-region as last resort. Also enforce a cost cap heuristic for cross-region spill.
Carlos: Operational constraint: some enterprise tenants rely on dedicated latency SLOs. If we route them to quantized variants without opt-in, SLA risk. Need tenant-tier exceptions.
Marta: Canary plan idea: roll new routing order for 5% of traffic (non-enterprise) with an egress cost cap. Monitor p95 latency, error-rate, and egress USD per 1k tokens. If p95>200ms or errors spike, rollback.
Josh: I'll own the canary rollout. Suggest ETA tomorrow 10:00 PT.
Marta: Core routing snippet for the router service prototype: 

```
route_preference:
  - local_dedicated: weight 100
  - local_quantized_variant: weight 80
  - local_shared: weight 60
  - cross_region: weight 10
cost_limits:
  cross_region_max_usd_per_1k_tokens: 0.50

# tenant_overrides: enterprise -> no cross_region unless explicit_allow = true
```

Priya: Also add billing tags when cross-region happens: so we can attribute egress to tenant and model variant. Enterprise tenants should have stricter rules (no automatic cross-region).
Carlos: For quota math: can't shrink dedicated slice sizes willy-nilly — that will trigger support tickets. We should instead allow temporary fractional shared-burst within region before cross-region fallback. Might buy us headroom.
Marta: Good point. So updated approach: 1) local dedicated (failover to smaller worker if configured per-tenant) 2) local quantized variant 3) local burst-shared (short-lived) 4) cross-region as last resort.
Josh: We'll need new metrics: spill_reason, spill_target_region, estimated_egress_usd. Add alert if cross-region spill_count > 5/min for top-50 tenants.
Priya: I'll add billing tags and a dashboard widget for top offenders. Also add a flag to route policy: allow_cross_region: true/false per tenant.
Marta: I'll draft the router PR and an updated runbook entry: "When dedicated pool saturates, prefer local degraded or burst-shared; avoid cross-region for production tenants unless approved."
Carlos: I'll run cost projections — rough calc shows avoiding cross-region for top 20 tenants could save ~15% of monthly egress bill for those accounts; will post numbers.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled -> router-service.canary namespace at 2024-11-05T17:00:00Z (initiated by Josh).
Josh: Thanks. I'll coordinate the canary checks and post the runbook link in this thread after rollout.
Marta: Thanks team — please ack if you see anything odd during the canary. :thumbsup:
